newsitem.title: ESTONIA: U.S. Omnitrax eyes Estonian rail company - paper.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Omnitrax eyes Estonian rail company - paper.

text.p: U.S. rail company Omnitrax is interested in buying a majority stake in the state-owned railway company of Estonia, the newspaper Aripaev on Friday quoted company officials as saying.
It quoted Denver-based Omnitrax president Dwight Johnson as saying his firm wanted to buy a majority in the company. The rest of the shares could later be sold on the stock exchange, he said.
He urged the government to speed up the sale of the railways, which need modernisation and made a loss of 2.3 million kroons last year on turnover of 270 million kroons, the Aripaev said.
The newspaper also said Omnitrax was interested in some parts of the port of Muuga, a key commercial port just outside the capital, Tallinn.
It said the U.S. firm was particularly interested in rail links from Tallinn to the northeastern city of Narva, on the border with Russia, as a transit corridor for Russian oil.
The Aripaev quoted the head of Estonian railways, Paarbo Juschnewitsch, as saying the privatisation plan should be ready by the end of the year and that he expected several bids.
